```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 5.5,
  dpi = 96
)
# the team ids below are checked against the team-index snapshot bundled with
# the package, so every build reads the same index
options(sdvplotR.offline = TRUE)
```

Three charts and a table from two European hockey leagues' 2025-26 seasons:
- the SHL's final table, built from every regular-season game;
- the SHL's points race;
- the SHL's goals for against goals against;
- the Ligue Magnus table in team colors.

The data comes from [fastRhockey](https://fastRhockey.sportsdataverse.org),
which reads the SHL's and the French federation's own data services. The team
codes and ids they return are the ones sdvplotR's team index keys these leagues
by. [Leagues and Identifiers](leagues-and-identifiers.html) lists what each
league's `team_id` is.

```{r setup}
library(sdvplotR)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)
```

## Load the season

```{r load-api, eval = FALSE}
# every 2025-26 SHL regular-season game
shl_games <- fastRhockey::shl_schedule(season = 2026) |>
  filter(state == "post-game") |>
  transmute(
    date = as.Date(start_date_time),
    home = home_team_names_code, away = away_team_names_code,
    home_name = home_team_names_long, away_name = away_team_names_long,
    home_score = home_team_score, away_score = away_team_score, overtime, shootout
  )
# the final 2025-26 Ligue Magnus regular-season table (phase 560)
magnus <- fastRhockey::magnus_standings(phase_id = 560) |>
  select(rank, team_id, team, games_played, wins, ot_wins, ot_losses, losses, points, goals_for, goals_against)
```

```{r load-api-fixture, include = FALSE}
fx <- readRDS("fixtures/euro-hockey-viz/standings.rds")
shl_games <- fx$shl_games
magnus <- fx$magnus
```

These calls are read from a snapshot taken on
`r format(fx$taken, "%B %d, %Y")` (`r fx$package`), because the leagues' data
services are not called when this site is built. `data-raw/article_fixtures.R`
takes it with the same code.

The SHL codes in the schedule (`FHC`, `SKE`, `ÖRE`) are the index's
`team_id`s, and so are the Ligue Magnus team ids. `sdv_resolve()` confirms
that every one is in the index:

```{r ids}
magnus <- mutate(magnus, team_id = as.character(team_id))
shl_teams <- sort(unique(c(shl_games$home, shl_games$away)))
c(
  shl = anyNA(sdv_resolve(shl_teams, "shl", id_system = "team_id")),
  magnus = anyNA(sdv_resolve(magnus$team_id, "magnus", id_system = "team_id"))
)

caption_shl <- "Data: SHL via fastRhockey | Viz: sdvplotR"
caption_magnus <- "Data: FFHG via fastRhockey | Viz: sdvplotR"
```

## Build the SHL table from the games

The SHL gives three points for a win in regulation, two for a win in overtime or
a shootout, and one for a loss in overtime or a shootout. One row per team per
game, then a sum:

```{r shl-table}
team_games <- bind_rows(
  transmute(shl_games, date, team = home, name = home_name, gf = home_score, ga = away_score, overtime, shootout),
  transmute(shl_games, date, team = away, name = away_name, gf = away_score, ga = home_score, overtime, shootout)
) |>
  mutate(
    extra = overtime | shootout,
    pts = case_when(gf > ga & !extra ~ 3, gf > ga ~ 2, extra ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  )

shl <- team_games |>
  group_by(team, name) |>
  summarise(
    gp = n(), w = sum(gf > ga & !extra), otw = sum(gf > ga & extra),
    otl = sum(gf < ga & extra), l = sum(gf < ga & !extra),
    pts = sum(pts), gf = sum(gf), ga = sum(ga),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(diff = gf - ga) |>
  arrange(desc(pts), desc(diff)) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number())

stopifnot(nrow(shl) == 14, all(shl$gp == 52))
```

## 1. The SHL's final table

A gt table with `gt_sdv_logos()` for the logos, and `gt_cutline()` under
sixth place (straight to the quarterfinals) and tenth place (the last place in
the eighth-finals).

```{r standings-table}
shl |>
  mutate(logo = team) |>
  select(rank, logo, name, gp, w, otw, otl, l, pts, gf, ga, diff) |>
  gt() |>
  gt_sdv_logos(columns = "logo", league = "shl", height = 24) |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = name) |>
  cols_label(
    rank = "", logo = "", name = "Team", gp = "GP", w = "W", otw = "OTW", otl = "OTL",
    l = "L", pts = "PTS", gf = "GF", ga = "GA", diff = "DIFF"
  ) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "SHL standings, 2025-26",
    subtitle = "Final regular season, built from all 364 games"
  ) |>
  tab_source_note(caption_shl) |>
  gt_theme_athletic() |>
  gt_cutline(after = 6) |>
  gt_cutline(after = 10)
```

## 2. The points race

Each team's points through the season, in its team color from
`scale_color_sdv()`, with its logo where the line ends.

```{r points-race, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, fig.alt = "Line chart of the 14 SHL teams' cumulative points over the 52 games of the 2025-26 regular season, each line in its team's color, with the team logo at the end of each line."}
race <- team_games |>
  arrange(team, date) |>
  group_by(team) |>
  mutate(game = row_number(), points = cumsum(pts)) |>
  ungroup()
# logos alternate between two columns past the last game, so close finishers do not cover each other
ends <- race |>
  filter(game == max(game)) |>
  arrange(desc(points)) |>
  mutate(x = max(game) + if_else(row_number() %% 2 == 1, 2.5, 6.5))

# the colour aesthetic goes on the lines only: geom_sdv_logos() would tint the logos with it
ggplot(race, aes(game, points)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = team), linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_sdv_logos(aes(x = x, y = points, team = team), data = ends, league = "shl", width = 0.035) +
  scale_color_sdv(league = "shl") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 52, 13), limits = c(1, 60)) +
  labs(
    title = "The SHL points race, 2025-26",
    subtitle = "Cumulative points, 3 for a regulation win, 2 for an overtime or shootout win, 1 for an overtime or shootout loss",
    x = "Game",
    y = "Points",
    caption = caption_shl
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

## 3. Goals for and against

Goals per game for and against, with each team's logo and the league averages
from `geom_mean_lines()`. The y axis is reversed, so the best teams sit top
right.

```{r goals-scatter, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, fig.alt = "Scatter plot of the 14 SHL teams' 2025-26 goals scored per game against goals allowed per game, each team drawn as its logo, with dashed lines at the league averages and the goals-allowed axis reversed."}
shl_rates <- mutate(shl, gf_pg = gf / gp, ga_pg = ga / gp)

ggplot(shl_rates, aes(gf_pg, ga_pg)) +
  geom_mean_lines(aes(x0 = gf_pg, y0 = ga_pg), colour = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_sdv_logos(aes(team = team), league = "shl", width = 0.07) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  labs(
    title = "SHL goals for and against, 2025-26",
    subtitle = "Goals per game, regular season (52 games); better defense is higher",
    x = "Goals scored per game",
    y = "Goals allowed per game",
    caption = caption_shl
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

## 4. Ligue Magnus points in team colors

The French league's final table as bars in each team's color, with its logo at
the end of the bar.

```{r magnus-points, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Horizontal bar chart of the 12 Ligue Magnus teams' 2025-26 regular-season points, sorted from most to fewest, each bar in its team's color with the team logo at the end of the bar."}
magnus_pts <- magnus |>
  arrange(points) |>
  mutate(team_id = factor(team_id, levels = team_id))

ggplot(magnus_pts, aes(points, team_id)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = team_id), width = 0.75) +
  geom_sdv_logos(aes(x = points + 4, team = team_id), league = "magnus", width = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_sdv(league = "magnus") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = setNames(magnus_pts$team, magnus_pts$team_id)) +
  labs(
    title = "Ligue Magnus points, 2025-26",
    subtitle = "Regular season, 44 games",
    x = "Points",
    y = NULL,
    caption = caption_magnus
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

## More leagues

fastRhockey also reads HockeyAllsvenskan (`ha_*()`) and the Czech Extraliga
(`elh_*()`). Their logos are in the index as `"ha"` and `"elh"`. Three
HockeyAllsvenskan clubs' codes in `ha_standings()` (`MORA`, `NVIF`, `ÖIK`)
differ from the index's (`MIK`, `NYB`, `OSIK`), so map those three before
plotting, until the index carries both codes.
